title: Encrypted Provenance Header and PII Minimalization Standard
author: Maya Patel
body:
Summary:
This standard defines a compact, encrypted HTTP header for passing minimal prompt and request provenance to downstream Redwood services for observability and audit, while enforcing PII minimalization and cryptographic controls. The header (XRW-Provenance) enables causal linking of inference requests across the edge-proxy, ingest-telemetry, and provenance-audit-service without exposing raw prompts or tenant-sensitive data in transit or logs.

Why this exists (Motivation):
- Current telemetry headers either leak too much context (raw prompts, user identifiers) or are too coarse to allow meaningful lineage and debugging.
- We need a single interoperable envelope that:
  - preserves the ability to attribute and trace requests end-to-end for debugging and billing,
  - does not contain plaintext PII, and
  - is cryptographically verifiable and revocable.

Scope:
- Applies to all Redwood public API frontends (edge-proxy), internal service-to-service calls that carry prompt/context, and Redwood Private runtime sidecars when configured to forward provenance.
- Not required for low-trust external webhook integrations; use the webhook-provenance adapter (separate doc).

XRW-Provenance header schema (compact table):
| Field | Type | Max size | Description |
|-------|------|----------|-------------|
| v | ASCII | 3 | Schema version (e.g., "1") |
| tid | UUID | 36 | Tenant ID (hashed, see PII rules) |
| pid | ASCII | 64 | Prompt-suite id or sanitized prompt fingerprint |
| rid | UUID | 36 | Request trace id (Redwood canonical request id) |
| ts | ISO8601 | 32 | UTC timestamp at generation |
| m | ASCII | 32 | Model identifier (catalog id) |
| q | small-int | 2 | Quality hint (0=low,1=normal,2=high) |
| sig | base64 | 344 | Signature (see crypto section) |

Note: The header value is a base64-encoded, AES-GCM encrypted JSON payload containing the fields v, tid, pid, rid, ts, m, q and then appended signature metadata. The plaintext size must not exceed 2KB before encryption.

Field semantics and PII-minimalization rules:
- tid: Must be a tenancy-scoped stable identifier. Production frontends MUST send the tenant id hashed using HMAC-SHA256 with the tenant-escrow key (hex, first 36 chars) to avoid raw tenant ids being present in intermediate logs.
- pid: Must never contain raw prompt text. Either send a deterministic fingerprint (SHA256 of normalized prompt, truncated to 64 chars) or a prompt-suite id (managed by prompt-catalog service).
- rid: The Redwood request id (UUID v4) generated at edge-proxy ingress and propagated with this header for causal correlation.
- ts: RFC3339 with second precision (e.g., 2026-02-10T15:04:05Z).
- m: Short model catalog id (e.g., rwd/gptx-7b-q4f). Do NOT include file paths or file-system artifacts.
- q: Quality hint selected by orchestration layer used by downstream fallbacks.

Encryption, signing, and key management:
1) Encryption: Payload MUST be encrypted with AES-256-GCM using a rotating provenance envelope key (PEK). PEKs are provisioned via Redwood KMS and rotated every 30 days.
2) Signature: After encryption, the edge-proxy computes an HMAC-SHA256 over the base64 ciphertext using a signing key derived from PEK and appends this as sig. Verification services MUST validate the HMAC before decrypting.
3) Key escrow and revocation: PEKs are stored in the provenance-key-escrow service. If a key is revoked, ingress will start stamping a new key id in the header and downstream services will consult the key-escrow for backward decryption for 7 days (grace window).
4) Local caches: Services should cache key metadata for up to 60 minutes and must refresh on HMAC verification failure.

SDK and server behavior guidelines:
- edge-proxy responsibilities:
  1) Normalize incoming prompt (trim whitespace, unicode normalize) then compute pid fingerprint; do NOT retain raw prompt in memory beyond the fingerprinting step.
  2) Generate rid if absent and add standard tracing headers (traceparent) in addition to XRW-Provenance.
  3) Build provenance payload, encrypt with current PEK, compute HMAC, and attach header. Header size should be <= 4KB total.
  4) Emit a structured metric: provenance.header.generate.latency_ms (p50/p95/p99) and provenance.header.size_bytes.
- ingest-telemetry responsibilities:
  - Validate sig; decrypt; verify ts within +/- 5 minutes of ingest time; if verification fails, increment provenance.invalid.count and drop decrypted payload.
  - Store only the fingerprinted pid and hashed tid in telemetry indices. Raw prompts must not be persisted here.
- provenance-audit-service responsibilities:
  - Maintain a short-lived audit cache (30 days) mapping rid -> (pid, hashed tid, model id) for fast incident lookups. Access to this service is RBAC-restricted and audited.

PII minimalization policy (service-level rules):
- Never include raw prompt text, user email, phone numbers, or other explicit PII fields in XRW-Provenance.
- If a downstream call requires a redacted excerpt for legal reasons, it must request a short-lived redact request to provenance-audit-service which will:
  1) Validate requester identity and justification,
  2) Produce a redaction token allowing decryption of a sanitized excerpt for 1 hour,
  3) Log the action with reason and approver id.
- Redaction false-positive/false-negative monitoring: maintain a weekly report of redaction-errors with target false-negative rate <= 0.01% and false-positive rate <= 0.1%.

Operational SLOs and thresholds (observability):
- Header generation latency at edge: p95 < 5ms, p99 < 15ms.
- Header size: median <= 512 bytes, 99th percentile <= 2048 bytes.
- Decryption/verification success rate (ingest-telemetry): >= 99.99%.
- Unauthorized audit access attempts: 0 tolerated; any attempt triggers incident process.

Monitoring and alerts (example):
- Alert: provenance.invalid.count > 1000 in 5m -> SEV2.
- Alert: provenance.header.generate.p99 > 25ms -> SEV3 performance review.
- Audit: provenance-audit-service.access.* logged to SEC-AUDIT sink within 1 minute.

Rollout and rollout safety steps (canary procedure):
1) Feature flag gated in edge-proxy (feature: xrw-provenance).
2) Canary: enable for internal-tenant(s) in us-west-2 only (1% of traffic) for 72 hours.
3) Monitor generation latency, verification success, and provenance.invalid.count; hold if any of:
   - verification success drops below 99.9% for 1 hour, or
   - provenance.invalid.count increases > 5x baseline for 30 minutes.
4) Expand to 10% across two regions for 48 hours, then to 50% and full rollout if metrics stable.
5) If a PEK rotation is in-flight, pause rollout until rotation completes and downstream caches refresh.

Developer guidance and examples (edge-proxy pseudocode):
- Example header generation (pseudo):
  payload = {"v":"1","tid":hmac(tenant_key, tenant_id),"pid":sha256_norm(prompt),"rid":req_id,"ts":now_iso(),"m":model_id,"q":1}
  ciphertext = aes_gcm_encrypt(PEK, json(payload))
  sig = hmac(derive_sign_key(PEK), base64(ciphertext))
  header_value = base64(ciphertext) + "." + base64(sig)
  set_header("XRW-Provenance", header_value)
- Example cURL (for debugging only; edge-proxy rejects raw prompt echo in headers):
  curl -H "XRW-Provenance: <base64cipher>.<basesig>" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate

Access control and auditability:
- provenance-audit-service endpoints require mfa + role:security.audit to decrypt or issue redaction tokens.
- All decrypt events are write-once logged to SEC-AUDIT with fields: rid, operator, justification, ts.

Testing and validation checklist (pre-merge):
1) Unit tests that ensure pid fingerprinting removes whitespace, strips emails, normalizes unicode.
2) Integration test: round-trip encrypt->verify->decrypt across edge-proxy and ingest-telemetry using test PEK.
3) Load test: generate headers at 10k rps for 30m; assert p99 generation latency < 15ms and decryption success > 99.99%.
4) Security review: threat model and SAST passed.

Operational runbook (incident-first steps):
1) If provenance.invalid.count spikes, open a SEV2 incident.
2) Identify whether root cause is key mismatch, clock skew, or header truncation.
3) If key mismatch, verify key-escrow health and roll back to previous active PEK if necessary.
4) For clock skew, verify NTP across edge-proxy fleet and adjust allowed ts window if appropriate.

Ownership and responsibilities:
- Edge-proxy team: implement header generation (owner: eng-infra/edge).
- ingest-telemetry team: validation, metrics, and decryption (owner: eng-platform/telemetry).
- provenance-audit-service: short-term storage, redaction flow, RBAC and audit logs (owner: security/forensics).
- Key management: platform-kms team (owner: eng-infra/kms).

Compliance and evidence:
- Evidence artifacts to collect for audits: key-rotation logs, SEC-AUDIT decrypt logs, canary rollouts and metric baselines. Retain decrypt logs for 3 years in restricted storage.

References and related docs:
- Prompt telemetry hash sampling playbook (see related_pages).
- Model prompt lineage spec (see related_pages).
- KMS key rotation policy (infra-standards/kms-rotation-policy-2025).

Appendix: FAQ and common edge cases:
Q: Why not send raw prompt encrypted?
A: We avoid encrypting raw prompt transit to reduce blast radius if a decryption key is ever misused and to minimize legal exposure; raw prompts, if required for legal, must be requested via redaction token.

Q: How do Private deployments adapt this standard?
A: Private runtimes may use a local PEK and local key-escrow; the header format and PII rules remain identical. Coordinate with security for key escrow integration.
